title: Smooth algebra homomorphisms lift across a henselian pair
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $S$ a smooth $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], $A$ a commutative $R$-algebra, and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal such that $(A,I)$ is a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Every $R$-algebra homomorphism $\tau:S\to A/I$ lifts to an $R$-algebra homomorphism $\widetilde\tau:S\to A$, meaning that the composite $S\xrightarrow{\widetilde\tau}A\to A/I$ is $\tau$.

proof.text: Write $\pi:A\to A/I$ for the quotient map and set $B=A\otimes_RS$, with structure map $a\mapsto a\otimes1$. By clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition], $B$ is a smooth $A$-algebra. The tensor-product universal property defines an $A$-algebra map $\sigma:B\to A/I$ by $\sigma(a\otimes s)=\pi(a)\tau(s)$: the formula is additive in each variable, $R$-balanced because $\tau$ is an $R$-algebra map, multiplicative on pure tensors, and sends $1\otimes1$ to $1$. In particular $\sigma(1\otimes s)=\tau(s)$. To apply the single-universe affine lifting statements without changing the universes of R, S, or A, use Algebra.FiniteType.small to regard B as a small type in the universe of A. Replace B by Shrink B, carrying its A-algebra structure along Shrink.algEquiv, and transfer smoothness and the section along this equivalence. After lifting, transport the resulting map back along the inverse equivalence.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] to $A\to B$: the smooth ring map obtained in Step 1 makes $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ smooth in the morphism sense required by the next lifting theorem.

source.place: Tag 0H74, application of Tag 07M7; affine smoothness comparison in Morphisms Tag 01V6 and More on Morphisms Tag 02H6

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-section-etale-lift] with its base ring $A$, ideal $J=I$, algebra $B$ and map $\sigma$. It gives an étale map $f:A\to A\prime$, an isomorphism $\alpha:A/I\xrightarrow{\sim}A\prime/IA\prime$ induced by $f$, and an $A$-algebra map $j:B\to A\prime$ with $qj=\alpha\sigma$, where $q:A\prime\to A\prime/IA\prime$ is the quotient map. All hypotheses are supplied by Step 2 and the construction of $\sigma$.

source.place: Tag 0H74, second sentence of proof; Tag 07M7, lemma-lift-section-smooth-morphism

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-henselization-stage-map] with its rings $(B,C,A)$ equal to $(A,A\prime,A)$, its ideals $(J,I)$ both equal to $I$, and $\varphi=\mathrm{id}_A$. The map $f$ is étale and its quotient map is the isomorphism $\alpha$ of Step 3; $I$ maps into itself and the target pair $(A,I)$ is henselian by hypothesis. Thus there is a ring map $r:A\prime\to A$ with $rf=\mathrm{id}_A$. This is an $A$-algebra map. The small representative from Step 1 and the etale algebra returned by Step 3 both lie in the universe of A, so this application respects the single-universe statement.

source.place: Tag 0H74, henselian retraction sentence using Tag 09XI, lemma-characterize-henselian-pair; Tag 0A02, lemma-henselization, final paragraph (single-stage section)

proof.text: Since $r(f(i)x)=ir(x)\in I$ for $i\in I$ and $x\in A\prime$, the map $r$ induces $\bar r:A\prime/IA\prime\to A/I$. The equality $rf=\mathrm{id}_A$ gives $\bar r\alpha=\mathrm{id}_{A/I}$, hence $\bar r=\alpha^{-1}$. Define $\widetilde\tau(s)=r(j(1\otimes s))$. The map $s\mapsto1\otimes s$ is an $R$-algebra map and $j,r$ are $A$-algebra maps, so this is an $R$-algebra map. Finally, for every $s\in S$, $\pi(\widetilde\tau(s))=\bar r(qj(1\otimes s))=\bar r\alpha(\sigma(1\otimes s))=\tau(s)$. This is the required lift.
